svg.title: The playbook in use: five phases, four roles
svg.desc: The playbook in use: five phases, four roles. Stages run across and lanes run down. What each role does in each phase, on one piece of work. Twenty cells, and between them the whole of what this playbook asks. Stages, left to right: Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis, Delivery and sign-off and Review. Analyst. Owns the method, the checks and the write-up. Engagement and scoping: Clarify the real question. Document the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions. Score the impact. Design: Choose the method. Plan the verification and validation the level asks for. Name your critical friend. Analysis: Do the work and your own checks first. Log decisions and assumption changes as you make them. Delivery and sign-off: Write it up with the caveats in the output itself. Produce the quality assurance statement. Review: Record the lessons where the next analyst will look for them. Critical friend. Independent advice on this one assignment. Engagement and scoping: Understand the brief, the context and how critical the work is. Design: Review the plan. Confirm the assurance planned is at the right level. Put your own time in the schedule. Analysis: Run the checks the level asks for. Report errors and improvements back. Delivery and sign-off: State the assurance: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented. Review: No action in this phase. The lessons recorded here include your Phase 3 findings. Commissioner. Owns the question and the decision it informs. Engagement and scoping: State the decision the analysis informs, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Score the impact with the analyst. Design: Approve the design. Make sure there is time and resource for the assurance the level requires. Analysis: Stay available. Review any change of design or method. Resist changing the question late. Delivery and sign-off: Confirm it meets your need, apply its limitations, and approve it for release. Review: Confirm whether it informed the decision, whether it is still used, and whether to decommission it. Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. Business Critical work only. Engagement and scoping: Named here. Confirm the status and the register entry. Design: Confirm that organisational governance procedures for design have been followed, before the analysis starts. Analysis: Stay aware of progress, and be available to approve at delivery. Delivery and sign-off: Review the assurance evidence, then approve as fit for its intended use. Review: Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose. How to read this: Read a row to see one role through the whole piece of work, and a column to see who is doing what at one moment. Level 1 work uses two of these rows: the analyst, and a colleague within the team as the critical friend. The fourth row applies only where the work is Business Critical. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.
